column1: # The `just cdyn` scenario: a program the *user* built with the recipe, linked against the
# shared C library, run in a standard image.
# Driven by `just test-cdyn-x86`, which is the only gate that goes through the recipe's own
# interface rather than `tools/build-dynlink.py` and `tools/build-dynlibc.py`: it runs
# `just cdyn tools/cdyn-demo.c`, injects the result with `MINIXFS_EXTRA`, and boots. The
# link underneath is `tools/cdyn.py`'s, the same one the shipped `/bin/dynclib` gets.
# One step per line, as `tools/smoke/scenario.tsv` documents: the command, a tab, and the
# whole line its output must produce.
# The expected output is `strerror(ENOENT)` from `libc.so`, reached through the loader,
# followed by the format conversions the engine carries. Nothing in `tools/cdyn-demo.c`
# computes that string, and `printf`, `open`, `strerror` and `errno` (a thread local in the
# object) are all resolved from `/lib/libc.so` at run time — so the line is evidence of the
# whole chain and not of one call. The gate fails if the program itself contains the
# The tail is the other half: no host test can reach `vformat`'s varargs, so this is where
# the floats (`0.1`'s exact expansion, the `2.5` tie rounding to even, `%e`, `%g`), the
# octal and `#` forms, and the `hh`/`ll` length modifiers are checked end to end.
